## Passages
RESULT [attribution]: Detects mislabeled data comparably to or better than exact influence computation on LoRA-tuned RoBERTa-large (GLUE). From the HTML version: 13 s for 4,500 influence computations vs 70 s for LiSSA and 11,279 s for exact, i.e. 5.5x and 1,149.6x faster on average.
US [attribution]: If increments are trained as LoRA or adapter deltas on a frozen detector backbone, DataInf is the cheapest way to rank the images in a new batch by influence on holdout loss. Its guarantees come from LoRA's small dimension, so they do not carry over to full YOLO fine-tuning. Use it only if the incremental design really freezes most weights.
CORRECTION [attribution]: Minor clarification: 13 s / 70 s / 11,279 s is for GLUE-QQP only, which is about 868x vs Exact. The 5.5x and 1149.6x figures are averages over the four GLUE datasets ('Across the four datasets, ours is 5.5 and 1149.6 times faster than LiSSA and Exact, respectively, on average').
